[[Atlie FC]] | matches = 240 | total goals = 631 | average goals = | league topscorer = [[David Radebe]] (17) | biggest home win = | biggest away win = | highest scoring = | longest wins = | longest unbeaten = | longest winless = | longest losses = | highest attendance = | lowest attendance = | average attendance = | prevseason = [[2010–11 National First Division|2010–11]] | nextseason = [[2012–13 National First Division|2012–13]] }} The '''2011–12 National First Division''' was the season from September 2011 until May 2012 of South Africa's second tier of professional [[association football|football]]. For the first time since the [[2003–04 National First Division]] season, all teams were placed in one unified league table. Previously the competition had been split into two 'streams'. == Summary == At the conclusion of the season [[University of Pretoria F.C.|Tuks FC]] secured their promotion to the Premiership after topping the table.{{cite news |url=http://www.kickoff.com/news/28396/matthews-welcomes-university-of-pretoria-to-the-premiership.php |work=Kickoff.com |date=14 May 2012 |accessdate=19 July 2012 |title=Matthews welcomes Tuks to the top-flight}} Second-placed [[Chippa United]] and third-placed [[Thanda Royal Zulu F.C.|Thanda Royal Zulu]] were joined by [[Santos Football Club (South Africa)|Santos]] of the Premiership in a three team promotion and relegation playoff. At the conclusion of the playoffs, Chippa United, only established in 2010, secured their promotion to the Premiership, in the process relegating Santos to the National First Division.{{cite news |url=http://www.mtnfootball.com/africa/south-africa/absa-premiership/news/2012/jun/chippa-promoted-santos-relegated.html |work=MTNFootball.com |date=30 June 2012 |accessdate=19 July 2012 |title=Chippa promoted, Santos relegated |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160312065054/http://mtnfootball.com/africa/south-africa/absa-premiership/news/2012/jun/chippa-promoted-santos-relegated.html |archive-date=2016-03-12 |url-status=dead }} This was Chippa United's second successive promotion as they had only just earned promotion to the National First Division. [[Atlie FC]] and [[Carara Kicks F.C.|Carara Kicks]] were relegated at the end of the season. [[Carara Kicks F.C.|Carara Kicks]] were only relegated after being deducted points for fielding an ineligible player,{{Cite web |last=OFM |title=Roses could return to the NFD |url=https://www.ofm.co.za/article/soccer/149395/roses-could-return-to-the-nfd |access-date=2025-03-07 |website=OFM}}{{Cite web |last=Matshe |first=Nkareng |title=PSL’s disciplinary process is flawed |url=https://www.iol.co.za/sport/soccer/psl/psls-disciplinary-process-is-flawed-1378536 |access-date=2025-03-07 |website=www.iol.co.za |language=en}} sparing [[Dynamos F.C. PSL Playoff Tournament]] |result2=QP|result3=QP |col_R=red1|text_R=Relegation to [[Vodacom League]] |result15=R |result16=R |update=complete|source= }} ==PSL playoff tournament== The teams that finished second and third during the ''2011-12 National First Division'' season were joined by the team that finished 15th in the [[2011–12 South African Premiership|Premiership]] season in a 3-team promotion and relegation playoff called the '''PSL Playoff Tournament'''. === Participants === {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: center;" |- !width="175"|Team !width"175"|League !width="20"|{{Tooltip|Pos|Position}} |- |align="left"| [[Santos Football Club (South Africa)|Santos]]||[[2011–12 South African Premiership|2011–12 Premiership]]||15th |- |align="left"| [[Chippa United F.C.|Chippa United]]||2011–12 National First Division||2nd |- |align="left"| [[Thanda Royal Zulu F.C.|Thanda Royal Zulu]]||2011–12 National First Division||3rd |} === Format === The 3 teams participated in a mini-league in which they played one another twice (home and away) with log points being awarded for winning a match (3 points) and drawing a match (1 point). At the conclusion of the mini-league phase the team that was in first place would either earn or maintain their place in the [[South African Premiership|Premiership]] for the [[2012–13 South African Premiership|2012–13 season]]. If the team that finished 15th in the Premiership was unable to win the mini-league, they were relegated to the National First Division for the 2012-13 season. === Playoff table === At the conclusion of the PSL Playoff Tournament [[Chippa United]] had topped the mini-league after defeating [[Santos Football Club (South Africa)|Santos]] 4-3 in the final game, earning their place in the PSL for the 2012-13 season. As they were unable to win the mini-league, ''Santos'' failed to maintain their place in the PSL and were relegated to the National First Division for the 2012-13 season. {{#invoke:sports
